question: Can a manufacturer-documented direct frame identity survive the X16 release and replace underidentified command-image inference?
confirmedFacts: The EoSens 3CL documentation offers an optional 32-bit counter in the first four pixels and increments it for each new image.
Two independent stream parsers decoded the same 95,504 L0002 frames and produced the same 48-byte-per-frame boundary record SHA-256 3f44e7d04842b0c10af4791a68ba9d109e17ce9ea885483249a628d203176e14.
None of the 24 sealed boundary, plane, and byte-order candidates contained even one adjacent difference equal to one; the gate required all 95,503.
Candidate sequences contained at most 80 unique values and at least 95,348 zero differences, consistent with mostly dark image corners rather than a counter.
The preregistered release failed, no L0001 bytes were acquired, and no natural missing position was called.

hypotheses.C0_counterAbsentOrUnrecoverable: supported for the released AVI under every sealed native boundary interpretation
hypotheses.C1_exactCounterPreserved: rejected by 0 of 95,503 required unit steps across all candidates
hypotheses.N1_allNaturalOmissionsInternal: not tested because L0001 remained sealed
hypotheses.N2_endpointResidualExists: not tested because L0001 remained sealed
hypotheses.N3_counterTransferInvalidOnNaturalLayer: not tested; transfer stopped in development

causalChainAdjudication.evidence: zero unit increments in every series

causalChainAdjudication.link: released marker to independent identity ledger
causalChainAdjudication.evidence: parsers agree on bytes, but no marker exists to interpret

causalChainAdjudication.link: identity gaps to natural missing slots
causalChainAdjudication.fastTest: frozen parser on L0001 with endpoint envelope

uncertaintyBudget.measurement: Both parsers share FFmpeg 7.1, so a common decoder transformation is not independently excluded.
uncertaintyBudget.model: Only the documented first-four-pixel mechanism and four orientation boundaries were tested; undocumented packing elsewhere was outside the sealed search.
uncertaintyBudget.sampling: Absence was demonstrated on L0002 and blocks transfer; it does not prove that every X16 layer or unreleased raw record lacks a counter.
uncertaintyBudget.endpoint: Even a recovered relative counter would require a start/end anchor whenever internal gaps sum to less than the aggregate deficit.
uncertaintyBudget.extrapolation: No statement is made about process defects, camera failure cause, radiometric values, or other builds.

minimumAdvance: The direct-key branch has been falsified in the actual released development layer without spending the 187,567,239-byte natural-holdout budget. This removes a tempting but unsupported path and preserves a precise acquisition requirement for future datasets.

nextDecisiveProgram.historicalDirectEvidence: Search NIST or author-held MotionBLITZ raw .dat, .exp sidecar, acquisition configuration, or trigger log for per-frame counters or high-performance ticks. Verify provenance before joining it to XYPT.
nextDecisiveProgram.historicalInference: Using XYPT only, select the closest toolpath-twin layer to L0001 before viewing its pixels. On that count-equal twin, preregister image-image multiscale and temporal descriptors, synthetic deletion gates, and an independent implementation before any L0001 release.
nextDecisiveProgram.futureAcquisition: Enable the camera counter, retain raw counter/tick fields, publish a trigger-frame ledger, and include endpoint anchors plus deliberate dropped-frame controls.

safetyEthics: The cycle reads public process data only, performs no actuation, handles no personal data, and makes no manufacturing quality or safety certification claim.
